key_insight: NeuROK introduces a data-driven generative model that produces realistic 4D object kinematics — temporally coherent deformations of objects under varied physical conditions — without assuming a fixed analytic physical model. It learns neural kinematic priors from data and generates physically plausible temporal dynamics conditioned on interaction or control signals.
problem_solved: Existing approaches to simulative 4D dynamics rely on predefined physical models and system identification, limiting realism and generality; NeuROK addresses the challenge of generative, realistic temporal deformations of objects directly from data, enabling flexible, controllable 4D synthesis.
method: Represent objects as 4D neural fields (space + time) that model shape and its temporal deformation jointly.
Train a conditional generative model that learns kinematic priors from observed trajectories, disentangling static geometry from dynamic deformation.
Condition generation on physical/control inputs (e.g., forces, interactions, initial state) and use physics-aware regularization to ensure temporal coherence and plausibility.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners with a flexible, data-driven way to synthesize realistic temporal object dynamics for simulation, data augmentation, animation, and robotics, removing dependence on hand-designed physical models and enabling broader generalization.
visual_elements: Before/after sequence: a short 3-4 frame strip showing static object → applied condition → resulting deformation over time.
Architecture diagram: block diagram showing 4D neural field + conditional generative module + control input pathway.
Latent interpolation grid: sampling different latent vectors to show variation in plausible kinematics for the same object.
Physics-conditioning schematic: icon-based flow illustrating control inputs (force/impact) mapped to dynamic output, with a temporal coherence indicator (e.g., smooth timeline).
paper_authors: Chen Geng, Guangzhao He, Yue Gao, Yunzhi Zhang, Shangzhe Wu
